transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I guess I'm here because of some trouble I've been having at the museum where I volunteer. People will be talking right to me, maybe about the next art walk or something... and I'll be looking right at them. But then I realize I just... missed the middle of what they said. I end up having to ask them to run it by me again. It's just... happening a bit too much.
Does this happen to you in other situations besides when you're volunteering at the museum?
I... I'm not really sure. I haven't paid much attention to it outside of that. Mostly just at the museum, I guess.
Do you think you're actually not hearing the words, or you're just not paying attention to what's being said?

I hear them fine. It's not my ears. It's just... like I was saying before, they'll be talking right to me, and I'm looking right at them... and I just realize I missed a chunk of it. I don't know where my head went. I just... have to ask them to repeat it.
Do you remember what was being discussed before you realized you missed a part of the conversation?
I don't really know. I guess... whatever they were talking about. I just know I missed it.
Does this happen to you when you're at home or with friends and family, outside of the museum?
I don't really know. Like I said, I haven't really noticed it much outside of volunteering. Maybe a little, but... mostly just at the museum.
Do you have trouble focusing when you're reading a book or watching a movie at home?

I guess sometimes with reading. Like... if I sit down with one of the gallery packets or some notes for the museum. I'll start out okay, but... after a few minutes, I realize my eyes are just moving over the page. My mind wanders off somewhere else. Then I just have to go back and read the same part over again.
Does your mind wander off when you're watching a movie at home?
Not really. I don't think so. Movies are... fine, I guess. I haven't really noticed it happening then.
Does your mind wander when you're listening to music or podcasts?
No, I don't think so. I don't really listen to podcasts... and music is just, you know, background noise mostly. So, no... I haven't noticed that.
Does your mind wander when you're doing quiet activities like puzzles or playing games?
I don't really do puzzles... or play games much anymore. So... no. Not that I've noticed.
Do you find your mind wandering when you're engaged in tasks that require your full attention, like work or chores?

I suppose. Sometimes if I sit down with... like a gallery packet or some notes, I'll start out fine. But after a few minutes, my eyes are just moving over the page. My mind kind of wanders off. I usually end up having to read the same part over again.
Do you feel anxious or stressed when you realize you've missed part of a conversation or can't focus on a task?
Not really. I don't... I wouldn't say I get anxious about it. It's just... I just go back and read it again, or ask them what they said. It's not really a big deal.
Are you having any trouble with your daily routine or responsibilities because of these episodes where you miss parts of conversations or your mind wanders?

Well... I suppose it's affected a few things. At the museum where I volunteer, the group has... they've sort of quietly shifted some of the planning pieces to other people. And... I don't really feel as confident leading the art walks anymore. Not like I used to. So, yes, a little bit.
Have you noticed any changes in how your friends and family interact with you since you started having trouble following conversations?
No... I don't think so. They just... talk to me the same as always, really. I haven't noticed anything different.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends and family since you started having trouble following conversations?
Well... like I just said, no. Things are fine with them. I haven't really noticed any difference.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?
No, not really. Just... normal, I suppose. I don't feel sad.
Have you been having any trouble sleeping lately?
No, my sleep is... it's fine. I sleep alright, I guess. Nothing out of the ordinary.
Have you noticed any impact on your job or other daily activities outside of volunteering at the museum?

Well, I don't work anymore. The museum is mostly what I do. I guess... well, the folks there have had to quietly shift some of the planning pieces away from me lately. And... I haven't really been leading the art walks the way I used to. I just don't feel as confident doing it, I suppose. But outside of that... no, not really.
Have you been experiencing these episodes of missing parts of conversations for a short period, like a few weeks, or has it been going on for months?

It's been longer than that. Probably... well, over two years now. Maybe two years and four months. That's when I had to take over the museum liaison duties all by myself. My... my friend passed away around then. It's just been causing more trouble since that happened.

You mentioned that your symptoms started around the time your friend passed away, do you think there's a connection between their death and when you first started noticing these episodes of missing parts of conversations?
I... I don't really know. I guess they just happened around the same time. I haven't really... thought about it like that.
Do you think the death of your friend had anything to do with you starting to notice these episodes of missing parts of conversations?
Like I just said... I really couldn't tell you. It was just around the same time. I don't... I don't really know how else to answer that.
